title: Olives, green, Manzanilla, stuffed with pimiento

content.title: About
content.content: Green Manzanilla olives stuffed with sweet pimiento are a classic Mediterranean delicacy. The olives are harvested while still unripe, then undergo brining and fermentation before being filled with finely chopped pimiento, giving them a bright aroma and a mildly spicy flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Manzanilla is one of the most popular olive varieties in Spain, known for its tender texture and delicate taste.
Stuffing olives with pimiento is a traditional Spanish tapa preparation.
Olives can be kept in brine for up to a year when properly sealed.
High polyphenol content contributes to the olives’ antioxidant properties.
In ancient Roman cuisine, olives symbolized peace and prosperity.

items.title: Rich in monounsaturated fats
items.content: Olives contain oleic acid, which supports cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Polyphenols and vitamin E protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber in olives promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Contains iron and copper
items.content: These minerals are essential for hemoglobin formation and energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Olives are suitable for low‑sugar diets.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Olives are often cured in salty brine, so people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Olive allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to olives or olive oil.

items.title: Possible additives
items.content: Check the label for preservatives if you have a sensitive stomach.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Manzanilla olives stuffed with pimiento make a great snack, add them to salads, pasta, pizza, or serve as part of a tapas spread. They can be eaten straight from the jar, lightly grilled, or incorporated into marinades.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep olives in their original brine in the refrigerator after opening. Properly stored, they last 2–3 weeks. If the brine dries out, replace it with fresh salty water.
